title: HINT for Clinical Operations — SOPs do not improvise
metaDescription: Keep operational protocols, routes, roles, checklists and cited sources together while excluding diagnosis, treatment and triage judgment.
h1: Your assistant drafts SOPs fast. HINT keeps it out of clinical judgment.
intro: HINT keeps operational protocols, roles, routes and checklists in plain-text notes beside unit documents. Your assistant reads the applicable approved source before drafting an operational step.

situations.before: A routing instruction is improvised from general medical knowledge.
situations.after: Every route needs an approved source
situations.body: The assistant points to the declared guideline and escalation role instead of deciding care.

situations.before: A handoff checklist drops one required step.
situations.body: The role, timing and required record travel with the checklist through every revision.

situations.before: One unit's protocol is applied in another unit.
situations.body: Hospital-wide policy can inherit downward while pharmacy and emergency-intake procedures remain isolated.

example.intro: The Sacred Heart demo grounds its emergency-intake operations protocol in SRC-1.
example.after: It drafts only the declared operational route, preserves the required escalation, and refuses requests for diagnosis, treatment or triage judgment.
example.compiled:
<protocol name="emergency-intake-1">
  Approved protocol grounded in SRC-1.
</protocol>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: Provide medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, dosing or triage decisions.
Invent a routing rule, clinical criterion or guideline.
Skip a declared step, red flag or escalation role.
disclaimer: For fictional demonstration and operational documentation only. HINT is not clinical guidance and must not be used to make care decisions.

faq.a: No. The vocabulary explicitly limits the assistant to operations documents and excludes diagnosis, treatment, dosing and triage decisions.
No. Your organization supplies and approves the sources that govern each protocol.
No. It can carry owner and review fields; your clinical governance process controls approval.

keywordDescriptions.protocol: Names an operational protocol, version and owner.
keywordDescriptions.sop: Defines a standard operating procedure from approved sources.
keywordDescriptions.checklist: Preserves a complete ordered set of required actions.
keywordDescriptions.record: States what operational information must be documented.
keywordDescriptions.role: Defines who is authorized to perform an action.
keywordDescriptions.route: Maps a declared condition to an operational destination.
keywordDescriptions.redflag: Triggers immediate escalation without making a diagnosis.
keywordDescriptions.deviation: Records how a departure from procedure is handled.
keywordDescriptions.training: States who must be trained on an approved procedure.
